company.name: Llobregat Express
company.business_model: Regional last-mile parcel carrier that receives parcels from e-commerce shippers, local fulfilment centres and partner carriers at a single cross-dock in the Zona Franca and delivers them across Barcelona and the lower Llobregat area: same day for shipments registered before 11:00, next day otherwise. It charges shippers per parcel by size and service level, and also works as the final-mile subcontractor for national networks that have no fleet of their own in Barcelona.
company.modeled_on: It works like the Barcelona metropolitan branch of a Spanish national parcel network such as SEUR, MRW, GLS or Correos Express. Overnight linehaul trucks feed one cross-dock, parcels are sorted by delivery zone before dawn, and salaried drivers run fixed zone routes in the morning, with a second afternoon wave for same-day e-commerce. Unlike those networks it has no national coverage of its own: it only delivers in the Barcelona area and takes parcels from shippers and partner carriers.
customer_segments: E-commerce retailers (fashion, electronics, home goods) shipping to consumers in the Barcelona metropolitan area
Marketplace sellers and local online shops buying same-day delivery
National parcel networks and couriers subcontracting final-mile delivery in Barcelona
Pharmacies and healthcare distributors (ambient-temperature goods only)
Retail chains and independent shops in Ciutat Vella, Eixample and Gràcia (store replenishment and supplies)
Offices and professional services in the 22@, Diagonal and Gran Via L'Hospitalet business districts
Industrial and spare-parts distributors in the Zona Franca, El Prat, Cornellà and Sant Boi industrial estates

hub.name: Llobregat Express Hub Zona Franca (BCN-ZF)
hub.address: Carrer 4, 18-24, Sector C, Polígon Industrial de la Zona Franca, 08040 Barcelona

service_promise.failed_delivery_policy: On a failed B2C attempt the driver leaves the parcel with a neighbour or building concierge only if the recipient authorised it in advance. Otherwise the recipient gets an SMS and e-mail notice (plus a card at the door) and the parcel returns to the hub. The recipient can book a free second attempt on the next working day in either window, or redirect the parcel to a partner pick-up point or locker. After a second failed attempt the parcel is held at the nearest pick-up point for 7 calendar days and then returned to the shipper. When a B2B recipient is found closed, the parcel is re-attempted automatically on the next morning's route.

seasonal_peaks.name: Black Friday and Cyber Monday week
Three Kings (Reis) gifts and January sales returns

zones.name: Ciutat Vella
difficulty_factors: Medieval street pattern in the Gòtic, Born and Raval: lanes 3-5 m wide where a van cannot enter or turn, so most stops are walked with a hand trolley 150-400 m from the vehicle

Camera-controlled restricted-access areas for non-resident vehicles in the Gòtic, Born and Barceloneta; registered goods vehicles may enter only in a morning loading slot (roughly until 11:00), so later stops are done entirely on foot
Large pedestrian streets (Portal de l'Àngel, Portaferrissa, the streets off La Rambla) and dense tourist crowds slow trolley walks all day
Perimeter DUM bays on Via Laietana, Ronda de Sant Pau, Paral·lel and Passeig de Colom are full from about 09:00; stays are limited to 30 minutes and must be registered in the areaDUM app
Old walk-up buildings without lifts or concierges, and many tourist flats with no one to receive, push up failed first attempts
Shops, bars and hotels open between 09:30 and 10:30, so B2B stops bunch up in the late morning

zones.name: Eixample
difficulty_factors: Regular Cerdà grid with chamfered corners (xamfrans) where most DUM bays sit: stop sequencing is predictable and one parking often serves 3-5 addresses

Superilla Barcelona green axes (Consell de Cent, Rocafort, Comte Borrell, Girona) and the Sant Antoni superblock: through traffic removed, 10 km/h limit, forced loops and loading only at designated bays
Heavy congestion on Aragó, Gran Via, Diagonal, Balmes and Passeig de Sant Joan at peak hours; stopping in bus and bike lanes is fined
DUM bays limited to 30 minutes through the areaDUM app; some chamfer bays are loading-only in the morning and revert to resident parking later, so afternoon stops take longer
Many buildings have a concierge (porter) who accepts parcels in the morning, which raises first-attempt success
Dense mix of shops, offices and flats gives several parcels per stop, but many shops only receive goods between 10:00 and 13:30

zones.name: Sants-Montjuïc
difficulty_factors: Nearest city district to the hub (La Marina borders the Zona Franca), so the drive to the first stop takes only 10-15 minutes
Sants, Hostafrancs and La Bordeta: dense blocks with narrow side streets; Carrer de Sants and Creu Coberta form a busy bus-and-taxi shopping street with few places to stop
Poble-sec climbs the slope of Montjuïc: steep streets and public stairways in the upper part, and very few DUM bays
Trade fairs at Fira Montjuïc and concerts and sports events at the Olympic Stadium and Palau Sant Jordi close streets around Plaça d'Espanya
La Marina del Prat Vermell: new developments with wide streets and easy parking

zones.name: Les Corts
difficulty_factors: Wide avenues (Diagonal, Travessera de les Corts, Numància, Joan Güell) and modern blocks with loading access and concierge desks
Diagonal office and retail cluster around L'Illa: mailrooms take large multi-parcel B2B deliveries
Pedralbes and the university area: low-density housing and campuses with gatehouses, so walks are longer and there are access checks
Match and event days at the Camp Nou close nearby streets and jam Travessera de les Corts and Arístides Maillol
Good DUM coverage along the Travessera de les Corts shopping street

zones.name: Sarrià-Sant Gervasi
difficulty_factors: Steep streets above Via Augusta (Bonanova, Putxet, Sant Gervasi, Tres Torres) with gradients over 10%: frequent hill starts and slow trolley work
Detached houses and gated blocks with intercoms and front gardens: long walks from van to door and more recipients not at home
Vallvidrera, Tibidabo and Les Planes on the Collserola hillside: winding roads that add 20-30 minutes, usually served once a day on a dedicated sub-route
Pedestrianised Carrer Major de Sarrià and narrow streets in the old village of Sarrià
School-run traffic around the many private schools blocks streets in Bonanova and Sant Gervasi from 08:30 to 09:15 and 16:30 to 17:30
Fewer DUM bays per street than in the Eixample; double parking on Via Augusta, Balmes and Muntaner is strictly enforced

zones.name: Gràcia
difficulty_factors: Tight mesh of narrow one-lane streets in the Vila de Gràcia, many of them single-level pedestrian-priority streets with a 10 km/h limit
Gràcia superblock: inner streets closed to through traffic, access loops only for residents, services and deliveries, and loading only at set places and times
Very few DUM bays inside the neighbourhood, so drivers park on Travessera de Gràcia, Gran de Gràcia or Via Augusta and walk in with a trolley
Upper Gràcia (Vallcarca, El Coll, La Salut) is steep, with stairways and outdoor escalators, plus tourist coaches and crowds around Park Güell
Small shops and bars open late in the morning; the Festa Major de Gràcia closes many streets for a week in mid-August

zones.name: Horta-Guinardó
difficulty_factors: Hilliest district: El Carmel, La Teixonera, Can Baró and Sant Genís dels Agudells have gradients above 15%, dead ends and stairway streets
Irregular street layout forces out-and-back sequences, and large vans cannot turn in many of the upper streets
Long drive from the hub, either across the city or via the Ronda de Dalt, which is congested at the Vall d'Hebron exits in the morning
Vall d'Hebron hospital campus: healthcare B2B deliveries with controlled access and security checks
Mostly residential, with few parcels per stop; street parking is easier than in the centre but DUM bays are scarce

zones.name: Nou Barris i Sant Andreu
difficulty_factors: Farthest zone from the hub (about 16 km): the drive via the Ronda Litoral or Ronda de Dalt to the Nus de la Trinitat takes 30-45 minutes at peak
Upper Nou Barris (Roquetes, Torre Baró, Ciutat Meridiana, Vallbona) sits on steep Collserola slopes with stairways and outdoor escalators
Avinguda Meridiana has been redesigned with fewer car lanes and limited stopping, and carries heavy traffic towards the Nus de la Trinitat
Sant Andreu de Palomar has a narrow old village core around Gran de Sant Andreu, and the La Sagrera station works cause shifting road closures
Flat industrial areas in Bon Pastor and Sant Andreu with wide streets, loading docks and easy parking for B2B
Many blocks have no concierge and online-shopping density is lower, so stops are farther apart

zones.name: Sant Martí
difficulty_factors: Flat Cerdà grid in Poblenou and the 22@ district with wide streets and newer DUM bays, so stops sequence efficiently
22@ technology district: offices and co-working buildings with reception desks give many parcels per stop, but receiving closes at lunchtime and after 18:00
Poblenou superblock: inner streets closed to through traffic at 10 km/h, with access loops
Diagonal Mar and Front Marítim residential towers with concierges and underground loading access
Ronda Litoral exits at Poblenou and Glòries congest in the morning peak; large music festivals at the Parc del Fòrum close roads in late spring and summer
Besòs i el Maresme and La Verneda: dense blocks without concierges and more failed attempts

zones.name: L'Hospitalet de Llobregat
difficulty_factors: Collblanc-La Torrassa and La Florida are among the densest urban areas in Europe: narrow streets with cars parked on both sides and very few DUM bays
Bellvitge and El Gornal: high-rise blocks with many flats per entrance; easy van access but long lift and doorstep times
Gran Via business district (Fira Gran Via, hotels, office towers, Bellvitge hospital) takes large B2B deliveries; major trade fairs such as the Mobile World Congress in early March jam the Gran Via
Very close to the hub (about 5 km via the Gran Via), so routes are compact and suit the afternoon same-day wave
Pedestrian and traffic-calmed shopping streets in the Centre and Collblanc

zones.name: El Prat de Llobregat
difficulty_factors: Flat, compact town with a regular street layout and a pedestrianised centre around Plaça de la Vila
Mas Blau business park and the ZAL Prat logistics area: B2B stops with loading docks, but with gate and security checks
The only road links from the hub cross the Llobregat (B-10/C-31 bridges), so a single incident there adds 20-40 minutes
Airport traffic on the C-31 and C-32B during the morning peak
Good kerbside parking and DUM coverage, with short distances between stops

zones.name: Cornellà de Llobregat
difficulty_factors: Mostly flat, with a regular grid in Almeda, Riera and Fontsanta-Fatjó
Almeda industrial and office area (large office campus buildings) with loading docks and many parcels per stop
Sant Ildefons: dense 1960s high-rise estate with many flats per entrance and scarce parking
Event days at the Espanyol football stadium and the nearby shopping centre jam Avinguda del Baix Llobregat
Recurring bottlenecks at the A-2 and B-23 access junctions in the morning peak

zones.name: Esplugues de Llobregat
difficulty_factors: Built on the lower slopes of Collserola: steep streets in the old centre, Montesa and Finestrelles; only the lower areas next to L'Hospitalet (Can Vidalet) are flat
Ciutat Diagonal and upper Finestrelles: low-density housing and gated developments with long walks from the van
Avinguda Laureà Miró (N-340) and the Diagonal/B-23 junction are heavy bottlenecks in the morning
Sant Joan de Déu children's hospital and corporate offices near the Diagonal: healthcare and B2B deliveries with controlled access
Low volume, so routes usually combine Esplugues with the western edge of L'Hospitalet or Les Corts

zones.name: Sant Boi de Llobregat
difficulty_factors: Longest drive from the hub among the neighbouring towns (about 12.5 km) via the B-10, C-31 and C-32/C-245, and the Llobregat bridge crossings are single points of failure
Flat town centre with a pedestrianised historic core and easy parking just outside it
Industrial estates along the C-245 and the river: bulky B2B parcels and loading docks, suited to large vans
Hillside streets around Marianao and high-rise blocks in Camps Blancs
Congestion on the C-245 (Carretera de Castelldefels) through Cornellà and Sant Boi at peak hours

avg_delivery_time_per_route_minutes.rationale: Measured for each route from the telematics geofence exit at the hub to the last delivered-or-failed scan, averaged over the 40 weekday routes (30 morning, 10 afternoon), including the 30-minute mid-route break. The 361-minute baseline is roughly 22 min from the hub to the first stop, 231 min stopped at addresses (about 72 stops x 3.2 min, i.e. stops_per_route x minutes_per_stop), 78 min driving between stops and the 30-min break. The 330-minute target (-31 min, -8.6%) comes from four changes: time-dependent stop sequencing (-14 min between stops), clustering stops around DUM bays so one parking serves several addresses (-8 min), staggered departures that avoid the Ronda Litoral and Ronda de Dalt peak (-5 min), and putting small vehicles in Ciutat Vella, Gràcia and the hill zones (-4 min). Every route stays under the 390-minute maximum, so morning routes that leave at about 07:40 finish by about 13:10 and afternoon routes that leave at about 14:40 finish by about 20:10, inside the 08:00-14:00 and 15:00-21:00 windows.

operational_risks: Morning congestion on the Ronda Litoral (B-10) and Ronda de Dalt (B-20), especially at the Nus del Llobregat and Nus de la Trinitat, between 07:30 and 09:30
Incidents on the few exits from the Zona Franca (Passeig de la Zona Franca, Gran Via, B-10 and the Llobregat bridges) that trap the whole fleet at departure time
Port container and logistics truck traffic in the Zona Franca and around the Mercabarna wholesale market overlapping with van departures
Private cars and other vans occupying DUM loading bays, forcing fined double parking or circling, with the 30-minute limit enforced through the areaDUM app
Street works and superblock or green-axis redesigns that change one-way systems and close streets at short notice

Mass events: FC Barcelona match days, the Mobile World Congress at Fira Gran Via, concerts at Montjuïc and the Parc del Fòrum, La Mercè in late September, the Festa Major de Gràcia in August and Sant Jordi on 23 April
Demonstrations and strikes (the Diada on 11 September, general strikes, taxi protests and farmers' tractor protests) that cut the Gran Via, Diagonal and ring roads
Rodalies commuter-rail outages that push commuters onto the A-2, B-23, C-31 and C-32 and sharply increase road congestion
Autumn rainstorms (DANA / gota freda) flooding underpasses and low-lying roads in the Llobregat delta
Summer heat waves that force adapted working hours and extra rest breaks for drivers and cut electric-van range because of air conditioning
Tourist crowds and cruise-ship days (coaches around the port, Drassanes and the Sagrada Família) slowing traffic and trolley walks
B2C recipients absent during working hours and tourist flats with no one to receive, causing failed first attempts and extra second-attempt work
Van break-ins and parcel theft while the driver is away from the vehicle, especially in tourist areas
Limited midday fast-charging capacity at the hub, and occupied public chargers, for electric vans that run both waves
